baseline_facts.content: Patient's name is Jack Smith.
Patient's date of birth is 31 October 1990.
Patient reports decreased hearing in the left ear for about six weeks.
Patient reports hearing difficulty only in the left ear.
Patient experiences occasional ringing in the left ear.
Patient has felt a bit sick a few times.
Patient has felt a bit dizzy a few times.
Dizziness is not severe.
Dizziness is not room-spinning.
Dizziness feels like being a little off balance.
Patient denies ear pain.
Patient denies chest pain.
Watching TV or listening to music alleviates the left ear ringing.
Patient does not use cotton buds to clean ear wax.
Clinician identified the patient's ear ringing as tinnitus.
A face-to-face clinic appointment for the patient is planned within the next four to five days.
The planned in-person visit will include examination of the patient's ear canal and eardrum.
The clinician does not consider the situation an emergency.
The clinician plans to exclude earwax impaction as a possible cause.
Patient is instructed to call the support team to schedule the clinic appointment.
The clinician will paste a link to a tinnitus leaflet in the appointment notes.
Patient is advised to book another appointment if issues arise before the clinic visit.
Patient reports a hearing problem about a year ago that lasted a couple of days.
